declarations.name: UiAccordionElement
declarations.description:
Show and hide sections of content from their headings.

Use the following composition to build a `ui-accordion`:

```text
ui-accordion
├── ui-accordion-item
│   ├── ui-accordion-header
│   │   └── h3
│   │       └── ui-accordion-trigger
│   │           └── button
│   └── ui-accordion-panel
└── ui-accordion-item
    ├── ui-accordion-header
    │   └── h3
    │       └── ui-accordion-trigger
    │           └── button
    └── ui-accordion-panel
```

Give every item a unique `value`. Put its trigger inside a heading, then add the panel it opens. The accordion's value is always an array of open item values, even when only one can be open.

The header wraps your heading and the trigger wraps your button. Use a heading level that fits the surrounding document. Tab moves between triggers; Enter or Space opens and closes their panels. Arrow keys, Home and End do nothing here: the APG removed them from the pattern, and a screen reader’s heading navigation already reaches each trigger.

Parts: `<ui-accordion-item>`, `<ui-accordion-header>`, `<ui-accordion-trigger>`, `<ui-accordion-panel>`.

Defined by `import "@ui-sdk/web/accordion"`.

Styling hooks: `data-disabled` (Present when the whole accordion is disabled).

attributes.name: disabled
attributes.description: Stops every item from opening or closing. Triggers stay focusable.

attributes.description: Whether closed panels stay in the page, hidden.

attributes.name: hidden-until-found
attributes.description: Keeps closed panels in the page as `hidden="until-found"`, so the browser's find in page can match their text and open them.

attributes.name: debug
attributes.description: Logs every change to the console, with its reason and what caused it.

declarations.name: UiAlertDialogElement
declarations.description:
Ask someone to confirm an action before you continue.

Use the following composition to build a `ui-alert-dialog`:

```text
ui-alert-dialog
├── ui-alert-dialog-trigger
│   └── button
├── ui-alert-dialog-backdrop
└── ui-alert-dialog-content
    ├── ui-alert-dialog-title
    ├── ui-alert-dialog-description
    ├── ui-alert-dialog-close
    │   └── button
    └── ui-alert-dialog-close
        └── button
```

Put the question in `ui-alert-dialog-title`, explain what happens in `ui-alert-dialog-description`, and wrap each answer's native button in `ui-alert-dialog-close`. Add `ui-alert-dialog-backdrop` to dim the page. Give the content and backdrop `hidden` to keep them hidden before the elements upgrade.

A Close part reports its `value` when it closes. `value="confirm"` is the agreeing answer that the [confirm helper](#confirm) recognizes.

Parts: `<ui-alert-dialog-trigger>`, `<ui-alert-dialog-close>`, `<ui-alert-dialog-shortcut>`, `<ui-alert-dialog-backdrop>`, `<ui-alert-dialog-content>`, `<ui-alert-dialog-title>`, `<ui-alert-dialog-description>`.

Defined by `import "@ui-sdk/web/alert-dialog"`.

Elements, CSS selectors, or a function that returns elements, read when the dialog opens. Presses on them never close it. In the attribute, separate values with commas.

members.description: The controller's methods, undefined until the element connects. `isOpen()`: Whether it's open. False as soon as it starts closing, while it still animates out. `setOpen()`: Opens or closes it. Returns false when the change was canceled or it was already open or closed. `open()`: Opens it, and resolves once it closes, with why, how and any return value. Resolves exactly once and never rejects: on the next close from any source, when `signal` aborts, or with reason `"unmount"` when the component leaves the page. `close()`: Closes it. `returnValue` is passed to the promise `open()` returned. Returns false when the close was canceled or it was already closed. `toggle()`: Opens it when it's closed, and closes it when it's open. events.description: Runs when the part is pressed, before the dialog closes. A returned Promise keeps the dialog open while it runs: the part gets `data-pending`, `aria-busy` and `aria-disabled`, screen readers hear the dialog's `pendingAnnouncement` after a second, and nothing but the controller closes the dialog. It closes with reason `"action"` once the Promise resolves. declarations.name: UiAutocompleteElement
declarations.description:
Suggest text while someone types, without limiting what they can enter.

Use the following composition to build a `ui-autocomplete`:

```text
ui-autocomplete
├── ui-autocomplete-label
├── ui-autocomplete-input
│   └── input
└── ui-autocomplete-content
    ├── ui-autocomplete-empty
    └── ui-autocomplete-list
        ├── ui-autocomplete-item
        └── ui-autocomplete-item
```

Name the input, then put suggestions in a list inside the popup. `ui-autocomplete-input` wraps a native input. Each suggestion needs a unique value.

Parts: `<ui-autocomplete-label>`, `<ui-autocomplete-input>`, `<ui-autocomplete-trigger>`, `<ui-autocomplete-clear>`, `<ui-autocomplete-content>`, `<ui-autocomplete-list>`, `<ui-autocomplete-item>`, `<ui-autocomplete-item-text>`, `<ui-autocomplete-item-icon>`, `<ui-autocomplete-group>`, `<ui-autocomplete-group-label>`, `<ui-autocomplete-separator>`, `<ui-autocomplete-empty>`, `<ui-autocomplete-status>`, `<ui-autocomplete-arrow>`.

Defined by `import "@ui-sdk/web/autocomplete"`.

attributes.name: container
attributes.description: Renders the popup into this element instead of in place, like a container inside a shadow root or an iframe. On web components, a CSS selector. Nested popups stay inside their parent.

attributes.name: value
attributes.description: The text. Pass it to control it.

attributes.name: default-value
attributes.description: The text at first, when uncontrolled. A form reset returns to it.

attributes.name: open
attributes.description: Whether the suggestions are open. Pass it to control them.

attributes.name: default-open
attributes.description: Whether the suggestions start open, when uncontrolled.

attributes.name: filter
attributes.description: How typing narrows the suggestions: `"contains"`, `"startsWith"`, `"fuzzy"`, a function of the item and the text, or `false` to keep every one, for results a server already filtered.

attributes.name: inline-complete
attributes.description: Whether typing completes the text with the first suggestion that starts with it, with the rest selected after the caret: ArrowRight or End accepts it, Backspace and Escape take it back out, and arrow keys fill in the suggestion they highlight.

attributes.name: auto-highlight
attributes.description: Whether the first suggestion is highlighted while typing, so Enter chooses it.

attributes.name: open-on-focus
attributes.description: Whether the suggestions open when the field gets focus, like recent searches, even before anything is typed.

attributes.name: submit-on-select
attributes.description: Whether choosing a suggestion submits, like a search box: `submit` runs, then the form submits.

attributes.name: status
attributes.description: Whether results are loading or failed, for the empty and status parts. Sets `aria-busy` on the list while loading.

attributes.name: loop
attributes.description: Whether arrow keys wrap from the last suggestion to the first.

attributes.name: modal
attributes.description: `false`: the page stays usable while the suggestions are open. `"pointer"`: an outside press only closes them. `true`: also locks scroll and makes the rest of the page inert.
attributes.default: false, or true while it presents as a sheet

attributes.name: presentation
attributes.description: How the suggestions present. `"sheet"` slides them up from the bottom of the screen with the field in its header, where they can be swiped away, and `"auto"` does that on small touch screens. A tap that opens a sheet leaves the keyboard closed until the field in the header is tapped. Decided each time they open; the server renders `"popover"` for `"auto"`.

attributes.name: disabled
attributes.description: Disables the field like a native input: it can't be focused or changed, and its text isn't submitted.

attributes.name: read-only
attributes.description: Keeps the field focusable and its text submitted, but stops changes.

attributes.name: required

type.text: { isOpen: () => boolean; setOpen: (open: boolean, options?: AutocompleteChangeOptions<AutocompleteOpenChangeReason> | undefined) => boolean; open: (options?: (AutocompleteChangeOptions<AutocompleteOpenChangeReason> & { signal?: AbortSignal | undefined; }) | undefined) => Promise<PopupResult<AutocompleteOpenChangeReason, never>>; close: (options?: AutocompleteChangeOptions<AutocompleteOpenChangeReason> | undefined) => boolean; toggle: (options?: AutocompleteChangeOptions<AutocompleteOpenChangeReason> | undefined) => boolean; getValue: () => string; setValue: (value: string, options?: AutocompleteChangeOptions<AutocompleteValueChangeReason> | undefined) => boolean; clear: (options?: AutocompleteChangeOptions<AutocompleteValueChangeReason> | undefined) => boolean; focus: () => void }

members.description: The controller's methods, undefined until the element connects. `isOpen()`: Whether the suggestions are open. `setOpen()`: Opens or closes the suggestions. Returns false when the change was canceled or it was already open or closed. `open()`: Opens the suggestions, and resolves once they close, with why and how. Resolves exactly once and never rejects: on the next close, when `signal` aborts, or with reason `"unmount"`. `close()`: Closes the suggestions. Returns false when the close was canceled or it was already closed. `toggle()`: Opens the suggestions when they're closed, and closes them when they're open. Returns false when the change was canceled. `getValue()`: The text. `setValue()`: Changes the text, which filters the suggestions. Returns false when the change was canceled or nothing changed. `clear()`: Empties the field. Returns false when the change was canceled or nothing changed. `focus()`: Moves focus to the field.

declarations.name: UiAvatarElement
declarations.description:
Show an image with a fallback while it loads or if it fails.

Use the following composition to build a `ui-avatar`:

```text
ui-avatar
├── img
└── ui-avatar-fallback
```

- `ui-avatar` shares the image's loading state with its parts.
- A direct-child `img` supplies the image. There is no image custom element.
- `ui-avatar-fallback` shows when no image is loaded.

The image is a real `img`, including in server markup. The browser can start fetching it before the elements upgrade. The fallback stays visible until the image loads; if loading fails, the fallback remains.

Parts: `<ui-avatar-fallback>`.

Defined by `import "@ui-sdk/web/avatar"`.

Styling hooks: `data-loading-status` (Where the image is: no image yet, loading, loaded, or failed).

declarations.name: UiCarouselElement
declarations.description:
Page through slides with native scrolling, keyboard controls, and optional rotation.

Use the following composition to build a `ui-carousel`:

```text
ui-carousel
├── ui-carousel-viewport
│   └── ui-carousel-content
│       ├── ui-carousel-item
│       └── ui-carousel-item
├── ui-carousel-previous
│   └── button
└── ui-carousel-next
    └── button
```

Put the slides inside a viewport, then add the controls you need.

The viewport is the scrolling window, and the content is the row of slides inside it, a flex row (a column when vertical). Name the carousel with `aria-label`, like "Featured products". Previous, Next, the indicators and the play toggle wrap your own `<button>`: give it text, or an `aria-label` when it holds an icon.

Parts: `<ui-carousel-viewport>`, `<ui-carousel-content>`, `<ui-carousel-item>`, `<ui-carousel-previous>`, `<ui-carousel-next>`, `<ui-carousel-play-toggle>`, `<ui-carousel-indicator-group>`, `<ui-carousel-indicator>`.

Defined by `import "@ui-sdk/web/carousel"`.

Styling hooks: `data-orientation` (Which way the slides scroll, and which arrow keys page), `data-playing` (Present while it rotates on its own), `data-paused` (Present while rotation is paused for now: hovered, the tab hidden, scrolled out of view or held. Pause a progress animation with it).

attributes.description: The current page, from 1. Pass it to control the carousel.

attributes.name: default-page
attributes.description: The page it starts on, from 1, when uncontrolled.

attributes.description: Whether it rotates through the pages on its own. Pass it to control rotation.

attributes.description: Whether it starts rotating, when uncontrolled. It doesn't when the user prefers reduced motion; the play toggle still starts it.

attributes.name: interval
attributes.description: How long each page shows while rotating, in ms. Hovering, a hidden tab and scrolling the carousel out of view pause it.

attributes.name: orientation
attributes.description: Which way the slides scroll, and which arrow keys page.

attributes.name: align
attributes.description: Where a page lines up in the viewport.

attributes.name: slides-per-page
attributes.description: How many slides one page holds: Next moves this many, and each indicator stands for this many. `"auto"` fits as many as the viewport shows.

attributes.name: loop
attributes.description: Whether the slides go round: Next on the last page goes to the first, which comes in after the last, and a swipe back from the first page reaches the last. With fewer than a page of slides to either side, Next on the last page scrolls back to the first instead.

declarations.name: UiColorPickerElement
declarations.description:
Choose a color by dragging across an area and along sliders, typing any CSS color, or picking a preset.

Use the following composition to build a `ui-color-picker`:

```text
ui-color-picker
├── ui-color-picker-area
│   ├── ui-color-picker-area-canvas
│   └── ui-color-picker-area-thumb
├── ui-color-picker-slider
│   └── ui-color-picker-slider-thumb
├── ui-color-picker-slider
│   └── ui-color-picker-slider-thumb
├── ui-color-picker-swatch
├── ui-color-picker-input
├── ui-color-picker-channel-input
├── ui-color-picker-eye-dropper
└── ui-color-picker-swatches
    ├── ui-color-picker-swatch-item
    └── ui-color-picker-swatch-item
```

Every part is optional, so use the ones your picker needs.

- **ui-color-picker** holds the value and is a group around the parts.
- **ui-color-picker-area** edits two channels, like saturation across and brightness up. A press moves the thumb there and starts a drag. Its background is `--color-area-background`, so give it a size and that background.
- **ui-color-picker-area-canvas** paints the area pixel by pixel, for channels no gradient can draw, like OKLCH's chroma and lightness.
- **ui-color-picker-area-thumb** shows where the color sits in the area. It's a slider that screen readers hear as both channels.
- **ui-color-picker-slider** edits one `channel`, like `hue` or `alpha`, drawn by `--color-slider-background`.
- **ui-color-picker-slider-thumb** shows where the channel sits along its slider.
- **ui-color-picker-swatch** shows the color, named for screen readers, like "vivid blue".
- **ui-color-picker-input** wraps an `<input>`, which reads any CSS color when you press Enter or leave it. Text that isn't a color goes back to the value.
- **ui-color-picker-channel-input** edits one `channel` as a number, in the units people read it in, like 0 to 255 for red.
- **ui-color-picker-eye-dropper** picks a color from anywhere on the screen, where the browser can.
- **ui-color-picker-swatches** and **ui-color-picker-swatch-item** are a list of preset colors.

Each part writes the color as `--color-picker-color`, so a thumb or a swatch fills itself with `background: var(--color-picker-color)`. The picker is form-associated, so it submits its value like a native input. The inputs, the canvas, the eye dropper and preset items use the `<input>`, `<canvas>` or `<button>` you put inside them, or make one.

Parts: `<ui-color-picker-area>`, `<ui-color-picker-area-thumb>`, `<ui-color-picker-area-canvas>`, `<ui-color-picker-slider>`, `<ui-color-picker-slider-thumb>`, `<ui-color-picker-input>`, `<ui-color-picker-channel-input>`, `<ui-color-picker-swatch>`, `<ui-color-picker-eye-dropper>`, `<ui-color-picker-swatches>`, `<ui-color-picker-swatch-item>`.

Defined by `import "@ui-sdk/web/color-picker"`.

Styling hooks: `data-disabled` (Present when the picker is disabled, by its own prop or a `<fieldset>`), `data-readonly` (Present when the picker shows its color but can't change it), `data-required` (Present when the picker is required), `data-out-of-gamut` (Present while a drag or a key holds a color outside the gamut. The value is the closest color inside, and the parts move there once the change commits).

declarations.name: UiComboboxElement
declarations.description:
Search a list of options and choose one or several values.

Use the following composition to build a `ui-combobox`:

```text
ui-combobox
├── ui-combobox-label
├── ui-combobox-input
│   └── input
└── ui-combobox-content
    └── ui-combobox-list
        ├── ui-combobox-item
        └── ui-combobox-item
```

Name the input, give each option a unique value, and put the options in a list inside the popup. `ui-combobox-input` wraps a native input. The label names the input; choosing an option puts its label in the input.

Parts: `<ui-combobox-label>`, `<ui-combobox-input>`, `<ui-combobox-trigger>`, `<ui-combobox-clear>`, `<ui-combobox-content>`, `<ui-combobox-list>`, `<ui-combobox-item>`, `<ui-combobox-item-indicator>`, `<ui-combobox-item-icon>`, `<ui-combobox-value-icon>`, `<ui-combobox-group>`, `<ui-combobox-group-label>`, `<ui-combobox-separator>`, `<ui-combobox-create>`, `<ui-combobox-empty>`, `<ui-combobox-status>`, `<ui-combobox-chips>`, `<ui-combobox-chip>`, `<ui-combobox-chips-overflow>`, `<ui-combobox-item-text>`, `<ui-combobox-select-all>`, `<ui-combobox-chip-remove>`, `<ui-combobox-arrow>`.

Defined by `import "@ui-sdk/web/combobox"`.

members.description: The controller's methods, undefined until the element connects. `isOpen()`: Whether the list is open. `setOpen()`: Opens or closes the list. Returns false when the change was canceled or it was already open or closed. `open()`: Opens the list, and resolves once it closes, with why and how. Resolves exactly once and never rejects: on the next close from any source, when `signal` aborts, or with reason `"unmount"` when the combobox leaves the page. `close()`: Closes the list. Returns false when the close was canceled or it was already closed. `toggle()`: Opens the list when it's closed, and closes it when it's open. Returns false when the change was canceled. `getValue()`: The selected value. `setValue()`: Selects a value, as a user would. A disabled or read-only combobox ignores it. Returns false when the change was canceled or nothing changed. `clear()`: Selects nothing and empties the input. Returns false when the change was canceled or nothing changed. `getQuery()`: The input's text. `setQuery()`: Changes the input's text, which filters the list. Returns false when the change was canceled or nothing changed. `focus()`: Moves focus to the input.

declarations.name: UiCommandElement
declarations.description:
Search commands, run actions, and open pages of more choices.

Use the following composition to build a `ui-command`:

```text
ui-command
├── ui-command-input
│   └── input
├── ui-command-empty
└── ui-command-list
    ├── ui-command-item
    └── ui-command-item
```

Give the input an accessible name and each command a unique value. `ui-command-input` wraps a native input. Keep empty and status messages outside the list, which holds commands and groups. The `action` event reports the value of the command that ran in `event.detail.value`; use it to perform the action.

Use `ui-command-group` and `ui-command-group-label` to name related commands, with a `ui-command-separator` between groups. Groups and separators disappear when filtering leaves them empty.

Parts: `<ui-command-input>`, `<ui-command-list>`, `<ui-command-item-text>`, `<ui-command-item>`, `<ui-command-shortcut>`, `<ui-command-page>`, `<ui-command-item-icon>`, `<ui-command-group>`, `<ui-command-group-label>`, `<ui-command-separator>`, `<ui-command-empty>`, `<ui-command-status>`.

Defined by `import "@ui-sdk/web/command"`.

Styling hooks: `data-loading` (Present while results load, with `status="loading"`).

attributes.name: value
attributes.description: The highlighted command's value. Pass it to control the highlight. `null` highlights nothing.

attributes.name: default-value
attributes.description: The command highlighted at first, when uncontrolled. Without it, the first command is, with `autoHighlight`.

attributes.name: query
attributes.description: The search text, which filters the commands. Pass it to control it.

attributes.name: default-query
attributes.description: The search text at first, when uncontrolled.

attributes.name: pages
attributes.description: The stack of open pages, from the first page opened to the current one. Pass it to control it. In the attribute, separate values with commas.

attributes.name: default-pages
attributes.description: The pages open at first, when uncontrolled. In the attribute, separate values with commas.

attributes.name: pending-announcement
attributes.description: What screen readers hear once a command has been pending for a second, so a slow action doesn't pass in silence. Set it in the page's language. An empty string says nothing.

attributes.name: filter
attributes.description: How typing narrows the list: `"fuzzy"` keeps commands with the text's letters in order, best matches first; `"contains"` and `"startsWith"` match the text itself. A function returns a score (0 hides) or a boolean. `false` keeps every command, for results a server already filtered. Composed commands keep their order, and data commands are ranked by score.

attributes.name: auto-highlight
attributes.description: Whether the first command is highlighted while nothing else is, and the best match as the user types, so Enter runs it.

attributes.name: loop
attributes.description: Whether arrow keys wrap from the last command to the first.

attributes.name: status
attributes.description: Whether results are loading or failed, for the empty and status parts. Sets `aria-busy` on the list while loading.

attributes.name: debug
attributes.description: Logs every change to the console, with its reason and what caused it.

members.description: The controller's methods, undefined until the element connects. `getValue()`: The highlighted command's value, or `null`. `setValue()`: Highlights a command, and scrolls it into view. Returns false when the change was canceled or nothing changed. `getQuery()`: The search text. `setQuery()`: Changes the search text, which filters the commands. Returns false when the change was canceled or nothing changed. `getPages()`: The stack of open pages, from the first page opened to the current one. Empty on the first page. `setPages()`: Replaces the stack of pages. Returns false when the change was canceled or nothing changed. `push()`: Opens a page on top of the current one, by the `value` of a `CommandPage` or a data command. declarations.name: UiDateInputElement
declarations.description:
Type a date one part at a time, in the order your user's language writes it.

Use the following composition to build a `ui-date-input`:

```text
ui-date-input
├── ui-date-input-segment
│   └── input
└── ui-date-input-segment
```

`<ui-date-input>` renders a group with one `<ui-date-input-segment>` for each part of the date: month, day and year in English, day, month and year in German. Each segment you type in holds an `<input>`. The slashes or dots between them are segments too, as plain text. The input renders its segments for you; give it a `<template>` only to change them, as in [Custom Rendering](#custom-rendering).

Parts: `<ui-date-input-segment>`.

Defined by `import "@ui-sdk/web/date-input"`.

Styling hooks: `data-disabled` (Present when disabled, by its own prop or a `<fieldset>`), `data-readonly` (Present when read-only), `data-required` (Present when required), `data-invalid` (Present while the date is before `min`, after `max` or unavailable), `data-empty` (Present while every segment is empty).

declarations.name: UiDatePickerElement
declarations.description:
Type a date or choose one from a calendar, with support for ranges and forms.

Use the following composition to build a `ui-date-picker`:

```text
ui-date-picker
├── ui-date-picker-input
│   └── input
├── ui-date-picker-trigger
│   └── button
├── ui-date-picker-hint
└── ui-date-picker-content
```

The input accepts a date, the trigger opens the calendar, and the hint describes the expected format. An empty content part renders a calendar for you.

Every Calendar part also works inside `ui-date-picker-content` and is defined by the Date Picker import. Write those parts out when you need to add styles, change the layout, or include custom day content.

An empty `ui-date-picker` renders the input, trigger, and calendar too. In range mode, it renders an input for each end. An input element wraps your native `<input>` or creates one. The trigger, Clear, and presets wrap a `<button>` or create one around their content.

Parts: `<ui-calendar-heading>`, `<ui-calendar-previous>`, `<ui-calendar-next>`, `<ui-calendar-month-select>`, `<ui-calendar-year-select>`, `<ui-calendar-grid>`, `<ui-calendar-weekdays>`, `<ui-calendar-weekday>`, `<ui-calendar-week>`, `<ui-calendar-day>`, `<ui-date-picker-input>`, `<ui-date-picker-trigger>`, `<ui-date-picker-content>`, `<ui-date-picker-hint>`, `<ui-date-picker-clear>`, `<ui-date-picker-preset>`.

Defined by `import "@ui-sdk/web/date-picker"`.

Styling hooks: `data-mode` (How the date picker selects), `data-open` (Present while the popup is open), `data-closed` (Present while the popup is closed, including while it animates out), `data-readonly` (Present when the date can be seen but not changed), `data-disabled` (Present when the date picker is disabled), `data-invalid` (Present when an input holds text that isn't a date, or a date that can't be picked).

declarations.name: UiDialogElement
declarations.description:
Open a focused task over the page.

Use the following composition to build a `ui-dialog`:

```text
ui-dialog
├── ui-dialog-trigger
│   └── button
├── ui-dialog-backdrop
└── ui-dialog-content
    ├── ui-dialog-title
    ├── ui-dialog-description
    └── ui-dialog-close
        └── button
```

The title names the dialog; the description gives it context. A dialog can have several Close parts, each wrapping its own native button. Give an icon-only close button an accessible name, as the first example does. Give the content and backdrop `hidden` to keep them hidden before the elements upgrade.

The backdrop is optional. Without one, style the content’s `::backdrop`. For a question that requires an explicit answer, use Alert Dialog.

Parts: `<ui-dialog-trigger>`, `<ui-dialog-close>`, `<ui-dialog-shortcut>`, `<ui-dialog-backdrop>`, `<ui-dialog-content>`, `<ui-dialog-title>`, `<ui-dialog-description>`.

Defined by `import "@ui-sdk/web/dialog"`.

attributes.description: Whether the dialog starts open, when uncontrolled. Focus moves into it once it's on the page.

attributes.description: Whether Escape, an outside press and Android's back gesture can close the dialog. Close parts, triggers and the controller always can. Pass `false` while a form has unsaved changes, and ask in `dismissattempt`.

Elements, CSS selectors, or a function that returns elements, read when the dialog opens. Presses on them never close it. In the attribute, separate values with commas.

type.text: { isOpen: () => boolean; setOpen: (open: boolean, options?: PopupChangeOptions<DialogOpenChangeReason> | undefined) => boolean; open: (options?: (PopupChangeOptions<DialogPayloadChangeReason> & { payload?: Payload | undefined; anchor?: Anchor | undefined; signal?: AbortSignal | undefined; }) | undefined) => Promise<PopupResult<DialogOpenChangeReason, string>>; close: (options?: (PopupChangeOptions<DialogOpenChangeReason> & { returnValue?: string | undefined; }) | undefined) => boolean; toggle: (options?: PopupChangeOptions<DialogOpenChangeReason> | undefined) => boolean; getPayload: () => Payload | undefined; focus: () => void }

members.description: The controller's methods, undefined until the element connects. `isOpen()`: Whether it's open. False as soon as it starts closing, while it still animates out. `setOpen()`: Opens or closes it. Returns false when the change was canceled or it was already open or closed. `open()`: Opens it, and resolves once it closes, with why, how and any return value. Resolves exactly once and never rejects: on the next close from any source, when `signal` aborts, or with reason `"unmount"` when the component leaves the page. `close()`: Closes it. `returnValue` is passed to the promise `open()` returned. Returns false when the close was canceled or it was already closed. `toggle()`: Opens it when it's closed, and closes it when it's open. Returns false when the change was canceled. `getPayload()`: The payload of the last open, from a controller or the trigger that opened it. `focus()`: Moves focus to the trigger that opened it last, or the first trigger.

declarations.name: UiDrawerElement
declarations.description:
A sheet you can open, drag, and resize from an edge of the screen.

Use the following composition to build a `ui-drawer`:

```text
ui-drawer
├── ui-drawer-trigger
│   └── button
├── ui-drawer-backdrop
└── ui-drawer-content
    ├── ui-drawer-title
    ├── ui-drawer-description
    └── ui-drawer-close
        └── button
```

The content is the sheet. The drawer positions it inside a full-screen viewport and moves it with `translate`. Give it a size, a surface, and corners; leave positioning and translation to the drawer. Give the backdrop a color, such as `bg-black/30`; the drawer manages its opacity. Give the content and backdrop `hidden` to keep them hidden before the elements upgrade.

Parts: `<ui-drawer-trigger>`, `<ui-drawer-close>`, `<ui-drawer-shortcut>`, `<ui-drawer-backdrop>`, `<ui-drawer-viewport>`, `<ui-drawer-content>`, `<ui-drawer-handle>`, `<ui-drawer-outlet>`, `<ui-drawer-title>`, `<ui-drawer-description>`.

type.text: { isOpen: () => boolean; setOpen: (open: boolean, options?: PopupChangeOptions<DrawerOpenChangeReason> | undefined) => boolean; open: (options?: (PopupChangeOptions<DialogPayloadChangeReason> & { payload?: Payload | undefined; anchor?: Anchor | undefined; signal?: AbortSignal | undefined; }) | undefined) => Promise<PopupResult<DrawerOpenChangeReason, string>>; close: (options?: (PopupChangeOptions<DrawerOpenChangeReason> & { returnValue?: string | undefined; }) | undefined) => boolean; toggle: (options?: PopupChangeOptions<DrawerOpenChangeReason> | undefined) => boolean; getPayload: () => Payload | undefined; focus: () => void; getSnapPoint: () => SnapPoint | null; setSnapPoint: (snapPoint: SnapPoint, options?: ChangeOptions<DrawerSnapPointChangeReason> | undefined) => boolean }

members.description: The controller's methods, undefined until the element connects. `isOpen()`: Whether it's open. False as soon as it starts closing, while it still animates out. `setOpen()`: Opens or closes it. Returns false when the change was canceled or it was already open or closed. `open()`: Opens it, and resolves once it closes, with why, how and any return value. Resolves exactly once and never rejects: on the next close from any source, when `signal` aborts, or with reason `"unmount"` when the component leaves the page. `close()`: Closes it. `returnValue` is passed to the promise `open()` returned. Returns false when the close was canceled or it was already closed. `toggle()`: Opens it when it's closed, and closes it when it's open. Returns false when the change was canceled. `getPayload()`: The payload of the last open, from a controller or the trigger that opened it. `focus()`: Moves focus to the trigger that opened it last, or the first trigger. `getSnapPoint()`: The snap point it rests on, or null before it first opens. `setSnapPoint()`: Moves it to a snap point. While closed, it opens there next. Returns false when the change was canceled or it was already there.

declarations.name: UiFileInputElement
declarations.description:
Choose, drop, or paste files, validate them, and submit them with a form.

Use the following composition to build a `ui-file-input`:

```text
ui-file-input
├── ui-file-input-trigger
│   └── button
├── ui-file-input-dropzone
└── ui-file-input-list
    └── template
        └── ui-file-input-item
            └── ui-file-input-item-remove
                └── button
```

The trigger wraps a native button that opens the system file picker. The drop zone takes files that are dropped on it or pasted while focus is inside it; keep a trigger beside it for people using a keyboard. The list copies the item in its `<template>` once for each file, and an item's `file` property holds its file; elements in the item with `data-file="name"`, `"size"`, `"type"` or `"path"` show that about the file. A remove button wraps a native button that removes its item's file.

Parts: `<ui-file-input-trigger>`, `<ui-file-input-dropzone>`, `<ui-file-input-list>`, `<ui-file-input-item>`, `<ui-file-input-item-remove>`.

Defined by `import "@ui-sdk/web/file-input"`.

declarations.name: UiHoverCardElement
declarations.description:
Preview a link on hover or keyboard focus while keeping its normal navigation.

Use the following composition to build a `ui-hover-card`:

```text
ui-hover-card
├── ui-hover-card-trigger
│   └── a
└── ui-hover-card-content
    └── ui-hover-card-arrow
```

The trigger wraps your own link (an `<a>`, so give it an `href`), and pressing it follows the link. The content is the preview, and the arrow is optional.

The card only adds a preview for people who pause on the link: everything in it should be reachable from the page the link goes to, since touch and screen reader users may never open it. For a tip on a button, use a Tooltip. For content that opens with a press, use a Popover.

Parts: `<ui-hover-card-trigger>`, `<ui-hover-card-content>`, `<ui-hover-card-arrow>`.

Defined by `import "@ui-sdk/web/hover-card"`.

type.text: { isOpen: () => boolean; setOpen: (open: boolean, options?: PopupChangeOptions<HoverCardOpenChangeReason> | undefined) => boolean; open: (options?: (PopupChangeOptions<HoverCardPayloadChangeReason> & { payload?: Payload | undefined; anchor?: Anchor | undefined; signal?: AbortSignal | undefined; }) | undefined) => Promise<PopupResult<HoverCardOpenChangeReason, string>>; close: (options?: (PopupChangeOptions<HoverCardOpenChangeReason> & { returnValue?: string | undefined; }) | undefined) => boolean; toggle: (options?: PopupChangeOptions<HoverCardOpenChangeReason> | undefined) => boolean; getPayload: () => Payload | undefined; focus: () => void }

members.description: The controller's methods, undefined until the element connects. `isOpen()`: Whether it's open. False as soon as it starts closing, while it still animates out. `setOpen()`: Opens or closes it. Returns false when the change was canceled or it was already open or closed. `open()`: Opens it, and resolves once it closes, with why, how and any return value. Resolves exactly once and never rejects: on the next close from any source, when `signal` aborts, or with reason `"unmount"` when the component leaves the page. `close()`: Closes it. `returnValue` is passed to the promise `open()` returned. Returns false when the close was canceled or it was already closed. `toggle()`: Opens it when it's closed, and closes it when it's open. Returns false when the change was canceled. `getPayload()`: The payload of the last open, from a controller or the trigger that opened it. `focus()`: Moves focus to the trigger that opened it last, or the first trigger.

events.name: openchange
events.description: Runs when the card wants to open or close. `event.detail.reason` says why, and `event.preventDefault()` stops it.

events.name: openchangecomplete
events.description: Runs once the card has finished opening or closing, after any animation.

events.name: payloadchange
events.description: Runs when the payload the content shows changes: a trigger with another payload opens the card, or takes the open card over, which fires no `openchange`, and so does a controller's `open({ payload })` on the open card. `event.preventDefault()` keeps the previous payload.

declarations.name: UiImageCropperElement
declarations.description: Choose the part of an image to keep by moving and resizing a selection, or by panning and zooming the image under it. Use the following composition to build a `ui-image-cropper`: ```text ui-image-cropper ├── ui-image-cropper-viewport │ ├── ui-image-cropper-image │ ├── ui-image-cropper-selection │ │ └── ui-image-cropper-grid │ └── ui-image-cropper-handle ├── ui-image-cropper-zoom ├── ui-image-cropper-rotate └── ui-image-cropper-flip ``` - **ui-image-cropper** holds the crop and the image's `src`, and is a group around the parts. - **ui-image-cropper-viewport** is the area the image shows in. Give it a size, and its padding keeps the image off its edges. - **ui-image-cropper-image** wraps your ``, with its `alt`, and turns and flips it. - **ui-image-cropper-selection** shows the crop over the image. It's a slider you drag or move with the arrow keys. - **ui-image-cropper-grid** draws lines across the selection, in thirds, for you to style. - **ui-image-cropper-handle** resizes the selection from one edge or corner, its `position`, like `"se"` for the bottom right. It goes beside the selection, not inside it, and sits on its edge or corner. - **ui-image-cropper-zoom** wraps a range input from 1, the largest crop, to `max-zoom`. - **ui-image-cropper-rotate** turns the image a quarter clockwise. - **ui-image-cropper-flip** mirrors the image left to right, or top to bottom with `direction="vertical"`. The viewport, image and selection are needed. The rest are optional. The zoom, rotate and flip use the `` or `

declarations.name: UiMenuElement
declarations.description:
Choose actions and settings from a button or a context menu.

Use the following composition to build a `ui-menu`:

```text
ui-menu
├── ui-menu-trigger
│   └── button
└── ui-menu-content
    ├── ui-menu-item
    └── ui-menu-item
```

Give items a `value` and handle the menu’s `action` event to run the selected command. A Group and GroupLabel can organize related actions; a Separator divides them without becoming a focus stop.

Pass a promise to `event.detail.waitUntil()` in the menu’s `action` listener or an item’s `select` listener to keep the item pending. It gets `data-pending`, `aria-busy` and `aria-disabled`, the menu stays open, and choosing it again does nothing until the promise settles. The menu closes once it resolves. A rejection keeps it open and puts the reason in the item’s `error` state until the next try. After a second, screen readers hear the `pending-announcement` attribute, “Loading” by default.

Parts: `<ui-menu-trigger>`, `<ui-menu-context-trigger>`, `<ui-menu-content>`, `<ui-menu-sub-content>`, `<ui-menu-sub-trigger>`, `<ui-menu-item>`, `<ui-menu-checkbox-item>`, `<ui-menu-radio-group>`, `<ui-menu-radio-item>`, `<ui-menu-item-indicator>`, `<ui-menu-group>`, `<ui-menu-group-label>`, `<ui-menu-separator>`, `<ui-menu-shortcut>`, `<ui-menu-item-icon>`.

members.name: api

type.text: { isOpen: () => boolean; setOpen: (open: boolean, options?: PopupChangeOptions<MenuOpenChangeReason> | undefined) => boolean; open: (options?: (PopupChangeOptions<MenuPayloadChangeReason> & { payload?: unknown; anchor?: Anchor | undefined; signal?: AbortSignal | undefined; } & MenuOpenOptions) | undefined) => Promise<PopupResult<MenuOpenChangeReason, string>>; close: (options?: (PopupChangeOptions<MenuOpenChangeReason> & { returnValue?: string | undefined; }) | undefined) => boolean; toggle: (options?: PopupChangeOptions<MenuOpenChangeReason> | undefined) => boolean; getPayload: () => unknown; focus: () => void }

members.description: The controller's methods, undefined until the element connects. `isOpen()`: Whether it's open. False as soon as it starts closing, while it still animates out. `setOpen()`: Opens or closes it. Returns false when the change was canceled or it was already open or closed. `open()`: Opens it, and resolves once it closes, with why, how and any return value. Resolves exactly once and never rejects: on the next close from any source, when `signal` aborts, or with reason `"unmount"` when the component leaves the page. `close()`: Closes it. `returnValue` is passed to the promise `open()` returned. Returns false when the close was canceled or it was already closed. `toggle()`: Opens it when it's closed, and closes it when it's open. Returns false when the change was canceled. `getPayload()`: The payload of the last open, from a controller or the trigger that opened it. `focus()`: Moves focus to the trigger that opened it last, or the first trigger.

events.name: openchange
events.description: Runs when the menu wants to open or close. `event.detail.reason` says why, and `event.preventDefault()` stops it.

events.name: openchangecomplete
events.description: Runs once the menu has finished opening or closing, after any animation.

events.name: payloadchange
events.description: Runs when the payload the content shows changes: a trigger or context area with another payload opens the menu, or takes the open menu over, which fires no `openchange`, and so does a controller's `open({ payload })` on the open menu. `event.preventDefault()` keeps the previous payload.

events.name: action

type.text: CustomEvent<{ value: string event?: Event waitUntil: (promise: Promise<unknown>) => void }>

events.description: Runs for every plain item, including items in submenus, with the item's value. Return a Promise to mark the item pending until it settles: it gets `data-pending`, `aria-busy` and `aria-disabled`, the menu stays open, and choosing it again waits. It closes once the Promise resolves, and a rejection keeps it open with the reason in the item's `error` state until the next try.

events.name: checkedchange
events.description: Runs when any checkbox item in the menu or its submenus toggles, with the item's value in `event.detail.value`. Made for data menus.

events.name: valuechange
events.description: Runs when any radio group in the menu or its submenus changes, with the group in `event.detail.group`. Made for data menus.

events.name: dismissattempt
events.description: Runs when `dismissible` refused a dismissal made on purpose: Escape, an outside press, back or a swipe. Focus or the window leaving is refused without it. Ask "Discard changes?" here.

cssProperties.name: --anchor-width
cssProperties.description: Width of the anchor, usually the trigger. Use it to match widths.

cssProperties.name: --anchor-height
cssProperties.description: Height of the anchor.

cssProperties.name: --available-width
cssProperties.description: Space beside the popup, up to the viewport edge. Not inherited either.

cssProperties.name: --available-height
cssProperties.description: Space between the anchor and the viewport edge. Use it for max-height. Not inherited, so a child that needs it copies it on the popup, like `[--list-height:var(--available-height)]`, and reads `max-h-(--list-height)`. The first popup registers both names for the whole page with `CSS.registerProperty`, so they don't inherit anywhere. A page that needs them to inherit calls it first, with `inherits: true`. An `@property` rule can't, since a registration in script wins.

cssProperties.name: --transform-origin
cssProperties.description: The point on the anchor the popup opens from. Use it to scale from the right place.

cssProperties.name: --arrow-offset
cssProperties.description: Where the anchor's center falls along the popup's edge, kept `arrowPadding` from the corners. Position a ::before arrow with it.

cssProperties.name: --drawer-progress
cssProperties.description: While it presents as a sheet: how far open the sheet is, from 0 closed to 1 at its largest snap point. Never past 1.

cssProperties.name: --drawer-dim
cssProperties.description: While it presents as a sheet: how dim the page behind is, from 0 to 1. The backdrop's opacity follows it.

cssProperties.name: --drawer-expand
cssProperties.description: While it presents as a sheet: 0 at the second-largest snap point and below, 1 at the largest. With one snap point, the whole travel.

cssProperties.name: --drawer-stack
cssProperties.description: While it presents as a sheet: how many sheets opened from inside this one are open above it, rising smoothly as each one opens. Push it back with it.

cssProperties.name: --sheet-backdrop
cssProperties.description: Set it yourself: the color the page dims to while it presents as a sheet. Black at 0.2 by default.

Use the following composition to build a `ui-menubar`:

```text
ui-menubar
├── ui-menu
```

Use the following composition to build a `ui-meter`:

```text
ui-meter
├── ui-meter-label
├── ui-meter-value
└── ui-meter-track
```

declarations.name: UiNavigationMenuElement
declarations.description:
Groups site links into panels that open from a row of triggers.

Use the following composition to build a `ui-navigation-menu`:

```text
ui-navigation-menu
├── ui-navigation-menu-list
│   ├── ui-navigation-menu-item
│   │   ├── ui-navigation-menu-trigger
│   │   │   └── button
│   │   └── ui-navigation-menu-content
│   │       └── ui-navigation-menu-link
│   │           └── a
│   └── ui-navigation-menu-item
│       ├── ui-navigation-menu-trigger
│       │   └── button
│       └── ui-navigation-menu-content
│           └── ui-navigation-menu-link
│               └── a
└── ui-navigation-menu-viewport
```

The trigger and the link wrap your own `<button>` and `<a>`, so they stay a real button and a real link. The list and its items take the `list` and `listitem` roles.

Give the navigation an `aria-label`. Each item holds a trigger and its panel, or a plain link. This follows the [disclosure navigation pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/disclosure/examples/disclosure-navigation/): buttons show groups of ordinary links. Use a Menu for actions instead.

The viewport holds the open panel and follows its size and position. Size it with `--viewport-width` and `--viewport-height` and clip its overflow when you use one; [Contents in the Viewport](#contents-in-the-viewport) explains the geometry. You can also [leave the viewport out](#without-a-viewport) and position each panel separately.

Parts: `<ui-navigation-menu-list>`, `<ui-navigation-menu-item>`, `<ui-navigation-menu-trigger>`, `<ui-navigation-menu-content>`, `<ui-navigation-menu-link>`, `<ui-navigation-menu-link-icon>`, `<ui-navigation-menu-viewport>`, `<ui-navigation-menu-indicator>`.

Defined by `import "@ui-sdk/web/navigation-menu"`.

Styling hooks: `data-orientation` (Which arrow keys move between the items, and where panels open), `data-nested` (Present on a menu inside another menu's content).

declarations.name: UiNumberInputElement
declarations.description:
Enter numbers, step through values, and format them for a locale.

Use the following composition to build a `ui-number-input`:

```text
ui-number-input
├── ui-number-input-scrub-area
│   └── ui-number-input-scrub-area-cursor
└── ui-number-input-group
    ├── ui-number-input-decrement
    │   └── button
    ├── ui-number-input-control
    │   └── input
    └── ui-number-input-increment
        └── button
```

`ui-number-input` holds the numeric value. `ui-number-input-group` wraps the text input and the optional step buttons. `ui-number-input-control` wraps your own `<input>`, and `ui-number-input-decrement` and `ui-number-input-increment` wrap your own `<button>`s, which change the value and repeat while held. Put input styles and accessible names on those native elements. `ui-number-input-scrub-area` is optional and changes the value as you drag it.

Typing updates the value when the text is valid and within bounds. Enter or blur commits it: the text is parsed, clamped, snapped to the step, and formatted. An empty input has the value `null`.

Parts: `<ui-number-input-group>`, `<ui-number-input-control>`, `<ui-number-input-increment>`, `<ui-number-input-decrement>`, `<ui-number-input-scrub-area>`, `<ui-number-input-scrub-area-cursor>`.

Defined by `import "@ui-sdk/web/number-input"`.

Styling hooks: `data-disabled` (Present when disabled, by its own prop or a `<fieldset>`), `data-readonly` (Present when read-only), `data-required` (Present when required), `data-scrubbing` (Present while a drag on the scrub area changes the value).

declarations.name: UiOtpInputElement
declarations.description:
Enter a one-time code with support for pasting, autofill, and native form validation.

Use the following composition to build a `ui-otp-input`:

```text
ui-otp-input
└── ui-otp-input-group
    ├── ui-otp-input-slot
    └── ui-otp-input-slot
```

`ui-otp-input` creates the native input and holds the code. `ui-otp-input-group` lays out a run of slots. Each `ui-otp-input-slot` displays the character at its place among the input's slots, or at its zero-based `index` if you set one. Add `ui-otp-input-separator` between groups when the code is easier to read in sections, like the dash in the example above.

Groups and separators change the presentation of one value. They do not create additional fields or tab stops: the slots display the value of a single native input, which handles selection, paste, undo, form submission, and autofill. It uses `autocomplete="one-time-code"` so supported browsers and password managers can offer a saved or received code.

Parts: `<ui-otp-input-control>`, `<ui-otp-input-group>`, `<ui-otp-input-slot>`, `<ui-otp-input-separator>`.

Defined by `import "@ui-sdk/web/otp-input"`.

Styling hooks: `data-complete` (Present while every slot is filled), `data-filled` (Present while the code holds any character), `data-disabled` (Present when disabled, by its own prop or a `<fieldset>`), `data-focused` (Present while the input has focus).

declarations.name: UiPaginationElement
declarations.description:
Navigate pages with buttons, links, or your router.

Use the following composition to build a `ui-pagination`:

```text
ui-pagination
└── ui-pagination-list
    ├── ui-pagination-item
    │   └── ui-pagination-previous
    │       └── button
    ├── template
    │   └── ui-pagination-item
    │       └── ui-pagination-link
    │           └── button
    ├── template
    │   └── ui-pagination-item
    │       └── ui-pagination-ellipsis
    └── ui-pagination-item
        └── ui-pagination-next
            └── button
```

Name the navigation with `aria-label`, then put the page links and steps in a list.

A list with a `<template>` renders the range from it: one copy for each page, with the page number in an empty button, and the `<template data-ellipsis>` for each gap. Without the ellipsis template, gaps get a plain `<ui-pagination-ellipsis>`. Links and steps wrap your own `<button>`, or an `<a>` with [`getHref`](#links), so style those. Links you write yourself, like a server's, take a `page` attribute.

The template keeps page entries keyed as the range moves. The current page's wrapped button gets `aria-current="page"` and `data-current`; an ellipsis shows “…” and is hidden from screen readers.

Give each step text or an `aria-label` on its wrapped button. At an end, the button gets `aria-disabled="true"` and `data-disabled` and stops changing the page. As a button, it stays in the tab order. Add `disabled` to `<ui-pagination>` to do the same for every page and step, like while results load. A controller still changes the page.

declarations.name: UiPasswordInputElement
declarations.description:
Enter a password, show or hide it, and use it in a native form.

Use the following composition to build a `ui-password-input`:

```text
ui-password-input
├── input
└── ui-password-input-toggle
    └── button
```

`ui-password-input` holds the value and visibility state. It connects to your native input and to the button inside `ui-password-input-toggle`. The toggle switches the input between `password` and `text`, and its button is a `type="button"`, so pressing Enter in the input still submits the form.

Put form options such as `name`, `form`, `required`, `disabled`, and `read-only` on `ui-password-input`. Put other native input attributes, such as `autocomplete`, `placeholder` or `id`, on the `<input>`.

declarations.name: UiPopoverElement
declarations.description:
Edit or explore something beside its trigger.

Use the following composition to build a `ui-popover`:

```text
ui-popover
├── ui-popover-trigger
│   └── button
└── ui-popover-content
    ├── ui-popover-arrow
    ├── ui-popover-title
    ├── ui-popover-description
    └── ui-popover-close
        └── button
```

The content has the dialog role. Its title names it and its description adds context. The arrow is optional, and a popover can have several Close parts. The trigger can live inside the popover or [connect from elsewhere](#triggers-outside-the-popover).

Parts: `<ui-popover-trigger>`, `<ui-popover-close>`, `<ui-popover-shortcut>`, `<ui-popover-content>`, `<ui-popover-title>`, `<ui-popover-description>`, `<ui-popover-arrow>`.

Use the following composition to build a `ui-progress`:

```text
ui-progress
├── ui-progress-label
├── ui-progress-value
└── ui-progress-track
    └── ui-progress-indicator
```

- `ui-progress-label` gives it a visible name. You can use `aria-label` on the root instead.

declarations.name: UiScrollAreaElement
declarations.description:
Add styled scrollbars, edge indicators, and follow-to-end behavior to native scrolling.

Use the following composition to build a `ui-scroll-area`:

```text
ui-scroll-area
├── ui-scroll-area-viewport
│   └── ui-scroll-area-content
└── ui-scroll-area-scrollbar
    └── ui-scroll-area-thumb
```

Put the content inside a viewport, then add a scrollbar for each axis you want to style.

The viewport is the real scroller. Give the root a size, and the viewport the root's full width and height. Scrollbars sit over the viewport's edges. A thumb appears when its axis overflows; [`type`](#when-scrollbars-show) controls when the scrollbar is visible. Render only the scrollbars you want: with none, the browser's own scrollbars stay.

The scroll-to-end part wraps your own `<button>`, so it keeps everything a native button does. The other parts are the elements themselves, and display as blocks.

Parts: `<ui-scroll-area-viewport>`, `<ui-scroll-area-content>`, `<ui-scroll-area-scrollbar>`, `<ui-scroll-area-thumb>`, `<ui-scroll-area-corner>`, `<ui-scroll-area-scroll-to-end>`.

Defined by `import "@ui-sdk/web/scroll-area"`.

Styling hooks: `data-overflow-x` (Present while the content is wider than the viewport), `data-overflow-y` (Present while the content is taller than the viewport), `data-at-start` (Present while the view is at the start: the top, or the inline start when only the horizontal axis overflows. Also when nothing overflows), `data-at-end` (Present while the view is at the end: the bottom, or the inline end when only the horizontal axis overflows), `data-at-x-start` (Present while the view is at the inline start, within a pixel), `data-at-x-end` (Present while the view is at the inline end, within a pixel), `data-at-y-start` (Present while the view is at the top, within a pixel), `data-at-y-end` (Present while the view is at the bottom, within a pixel), `data-scrolling` (Present while the user scrolls, and for a moment after. Keeping the end in view doesn't count), `data-hovering` (Present while a mouse or pen is over the scroll area), `data-sticking` (Present while the view follows the end as content grows, with `stickToEnd`).

attributes.description: When the scrollbars show: "auto" whenever the content overflows, "always" even when it doesn't, "scroll" while scrolling, and "hover" while scrolling or while the pointer is over the scroll area. Each scrollbar has `data-visible` while it should show; style that.

attributes.name: scroll-hide-delay
attributes.description: How long scrollbars stay after they stop being needed, in ms, with "scroll" and "hover".

attributes.name: stick-to-end
attributes.description: Keeps the end in view while the content grows, like a chat or streamed output: it starts at the bottom and stays there. Scrolling toward the top lets go, and scrolling back to the bottom sticks again.

declarations.name: UiSelectElement

Use the following composition to build a `ui-select`:

```text
ui-select
├── ui-select-label
├── ui-select-trigger
│   └── button
│       └── ui-select-value
└── ui-select-content
    ├── ui-select-item
    └── ui-select-item
```

Start with a label, a trigger, and a list of items. `ui-select-value` shows the selected item's label inside the trigger. `ui-select-label` names the trigger; inside a Field, use its `ui-field-label` instead, as the examples do.

Parts: `<ui-select-label>`, `<ui-select-trigger>`, `<ui-select-value>`, `<ui-select-clear>`, `<ui-select-content>`, `<ui-select-list>`, `<ui-select-input>`, `<ui-select-empty>`, `<ui-select-status>`, `<ui-select-item-text>`, `<ui-select-select-all>`, `<ui-select-item>`, `<ui-select-item-indicator>`, `<ui-select-item-icon>`, `<ui-select-value-icon>`, `<ui-select-group>`, `<ui-select-group-label>`, `<ui-select-separator>`, `<ui-select-arrow>`.

type.text: false | "startsWith" | "contains" | (item: ListItem<any>, query: string) => number | boolean

members.name: virtualFocus
members.description: Keeps focus on the trigger while the list is open, as on a native select: arrow keys, Home, End and typing move the highlight, and the trigger points at the highlighted item with `aria-activedescendant`. A search field in the list still takes focus.

members.name: modal
members.description: `"pointer"`: an outside press only closes the list. `true`: also locks scroll and makes the rest of the page inert. `false`: outside presses reach what they hit.

members.name: presentation
members.description: How the list presents. `"sheet"` slides it up from the bottom of the screen, where it can be swiped away, and `"auto"` does that on small touch screens. Decided each time it opens; the server renders `"popover"` for `"auto"`.

members.name: disabled

members.name: readOnly

members.name: required
members.description: Blocks form submission until a value is selected, with the browser's own message.

members.name: autoComplete
members.description: A hint for the browser's autofill, like `"country"`.

members.name: dismissible
members.description: Whether Escape, an outside press, focus or the window leaving, Android's back gesture and a sheet's swipe can close it. Triggers, Close parts and the controller always can. Pass `false` while it holds unsaved work, and ask in `dismissattempt`.

members.name: debug
members.description: Logs every change to the console, with its reason and what caused it.

members.name: api

type.text: { isOpen: () => boolean; setOpen: (open: boolean, options?: SelectChangeOptions<SelectOpenChangeReason> | undefined) => boolean; open: (options?: (SelectChangeOptions<SelectOpenChangeReason> & { signal?: AbortSignal | undefined; }) | undefined) => Promise<PopupResult<SelectOpenChangeReason, never>>; close: (options?: SelectChangeOptions<SelectOpenChangeReason> | undefined) => boolean; toggle: (options?: SelectChangeOptions<SelectOpenChangeReason> | undefined) => boolean; getValue: () => unknown; setValue: (value: unknown, options?: SelectChangeOptions<SelectValueChangeReason> | undefined) => boolean; clear: (options?: SelectChangeOptions<SelectValueChangeReason> | undefined) => boolean; getQuery: () => string; setQuery: (query: string, options?: SelectChangeOptions<SelectQueryChangeReason> | undefined) => boolean; focus: () => void }

members.description: The controller's methods, undefined until the element connects. `isOpen()`: Whether the list is open. `setOpen()`: Opens or closes the list. Returns false when the change was canceled or it was already open or closed. `open()`: Opens the list, and resolves once it closes, with why and how. Resolves exactly once and never rejects: on the next close from any source, when `signal` aborts, or with reason `"unmount"` when the select leaves the page. `close()`: Closes the list. Returns false when the close was canceled or it was already closed. `toggle()`: Opens the list when it's closed, and closes it when it's open. Returns false when the change was canceled. `getValue()`: The selected value. `setValue()`: Selects a value, as a user would. A disabled or read-only select ignores it. Returns false when the change was canceled, ignored or the value was already selected. `clear()`: Selects nothing: `null`, or an empty list with `multiple`. Returns false when nothing changed. `getQuery()`: The text in the search field. `setQuery()`: Changes the text in the search field, which filters the list. Returns false when nothing changed. `focus()`: Moves focus to the trigger.

members.name: checkValidity
members.description: Whether its value is valid. When it isn't, fires `invalid` on it.

members.name: reportValidity
members.description: Whether its value is valid. When it isn't, fires `invalid` on it and shows the browser's message.

members.name: setCustomValidity
members.description: Makes its value invalid with this message, or valid again with an empty string.

events.name: openchange
events.description: Runs when the list wants to open or close. `event.detail.reason` says why, and `event.preventDefault()` stops it.

events.name: openchangecomplete
events.description: Runs once the list has finished opening or closing, after any animation.

events.name: querychange
events.description: Runs when the search field's text wants to change: typing, or closing the list, which empties it.

events.name: loadmore
events.description: Runs when the highlight or scrolling reaches the last item, so the next page can load, like `createAsyncOptions`'s `loadMore`. Not again for the same items, unless the last load failed.

events.name: highlight
events.description: Runs when the highlight moves, with the item's index among the visible items, so a virtualized list can scroll to it.

events.name: dismissattempt
events.description: Runs when `dismissible` refused a dismissal made on purpose: Escape, an outside press, back or a swipe. Focus or the window leaving is refused without it. Ask "Discard changes?" here.

events.name: valuechange
events.description: Runs when a user, a form reset or a controller wants to change the value. `event.detail.reason` says why, and `event.preventDefault()` stops it.

cssProperties.description: Height of the anchor.

cssProperties.name: --available-width
cssProperties.description: Space beside the popup, up to the viewport edge. Not inherited either.

cssProperties.name: --available-height
cssProperties.description: Space between the anchor and the viewport edge. Use it for max-height. Not inherited, so a child that needs it copies it on the popup, like `[--list-height:var(--available-height)]`, and reads `max-h-(--list-height)`. The first popup registers both names for the whole page with `CSS.registerProperty`, so they don't inherit anywhere. A page that needs them to inherit calls it first, with `inherits: true`. An `@property` rule can't, since a registration in script wins.

cssProperties.description: The point on the anchor the popup opens from. Use it to scale from the right place.

cssProperties.name: --arrow-offset

cssProperties.name: --drawer-expand
cssProperties.description: While it presents as a sheet: 0 at the second-largest snap point and below, 1 at the largest. With one snap point, the whole travel.

cssProperties.name: --drawer-stack

declarations.name: UiSliderElement
declarations.description:
Adjust a number or a range with draggable thumbs and keyboard controls.

Use the following composition to build a `ui-slider`:

```text
ui-slider
├── ui-slider-value
└── ui-slider-control
    └── ui-slider-track
        ├── ui-slider-indicator
        └── ui-slider-thumb
```

A control handles presses around the track. Put a thumb on that track for each value.

- **ui-slider** holds the value and is a group around the thumbs.
- **ui-slider-control** is where presses land. Pressing it moves the nearest thumb and starts a drag. Give it some height around a thin track.
- **ui-slider-track** is the rail the thumbs move along. Thumbs and the indicator are placed in percentages of it with inline styles, so give it a size. It's the positioned box.
- **ui-slider-indicator** fills the track up to a single thumb, or between the first and last thumb of a range.
- **ui-slider-thumb** is what you drag. Give each one a size.
- **ui-slider-value** shows the formatted value, and a range joined with an en dash. It's optional.

Each thumb renders a visually hidden `<input type="range">` inside itself. That input is what takes focus, so
screen readers on phones adjust it with their own gestures. Style focus on the thumb with `:has(:focus-visible)`.
`<ui-slider>` is form-associated, so it is what the form sees. An empty `<ui-slider-value>` shows the
formatted value.

A single thumb is named by a `ui-field-label` in a `ui-field`, or by `aria-label` on the thumb. In a range, give
each thumb its own `aria-label`, like "Minimum price", and name the group with a `ui-field-label` or
`aria-label` on the slider.

Parts: `<ui-slider-control>`, `<ui-slider-track>`, `<ui-slider-indicator>`, `<ui-slider-thumb>`, `<ui-slider-thumb-input>`, `<ui-slider-value>`.

Defined by `import "@ui-sdk/web/slider"`.

Styling hooks: `data-orientation` (The slider's axis), `data-disabled` (Present when disabled, by its own prop or a `<fieldset>`), `data-dragging` (Present while a thumb is being dragged).

```text
ui-tabs
├── ui-tabs-list
│   ├── ui-tabs-tab
│   │   └── button
│   └── ui-tabs-tab
```

Use the following composition to build a `ui-toggle`:

```text
ui-toggle
└── button
    └── ui-toggle-icon
```

And a `ui-toggle-group`:

```text
ui-toggle-group
├── ui-toggle
│   └── button
│       └── ui-toggle-icon
└── ui-toggle
    └── button
```

`ui-toggle` wraps a native button, which reports its state with `aria-pressed`. `ui-toggle-icon` is optional: it holds an icon and hides it from screen readers. In a group, give each toggle a `value`; the group's value lists the pressed ones.

```text

├── ui-toolbar-button

├── ui-toolbar-group
```

declarations.name: UiTooltipElement
declarations.description:
Name a control or add a short hint on hover and keyboard focus.

Use the following composition to build a `ui-tooltip`:

```text
ui-tooltip
├── ui-tooltip-trigger
│   └── button
└── ui-tooltip-content
    ├── ui-tooltip-arrow
    └── ui-tooltip-shortcut
```

Wrap the trigger and its hint in a tooltip. The trigger wraps your own `<button>` or link, so it keeps everything a native button does. The arrow and the shortcut are optional.

The content has the `tooltip` role, and it's in the page from the start, hidden, so it names or describes its trigger before focus reaches it. It names a trigger without a name of its own, like a button with only an icon, and describes any other: one with text, an `aria-label` or a `title`. `type="label"` or `type="description"` overrides the guess. Keep it to plain text: a tooltip can't be focused, so links or buttons inside it can't be reached. For anything interactive, use a Popover or a Hover Card.

declarations.name: UiTreeElement
declarations.description:
Browse a hierarchy of files, pages, or choices with expandable branches.

Use the following composition to build a `ui-tree`:

```text
ui-tree
├── ui-tree-item
│   ├── ui-tree-item-label
│   │   └── ui-tree-item-indicator
│   └── ui-tree-group
│       └── ui-tree-item
│           └── ui-tree-item-label
└── ui-tree-item
    └── ui-tree-item-label
```

Give the tree an accessible name and every item a unique `value`. An item with a `ui-tree-group` inside it is a branch. The group holds its children; the label names the item. The indicator and checkbox are optional, and they belong to the item around them, so put them inside its label to make them part of the row.

Parts: `<ui-tree-item>`, `<ui-tree-item-label>`, `<ui-tree-item-indicator>`, `<ui-tree-item-checkbox>`, `<ui-tree-group>`.

Defined by `import "@ui-sdk/web/tree"`.

declarations.name: UiTriggerMenuElement
declarations.description:
"Opens suggestions at the caret when you type a trigger such as @, /, or #."

Use the following composition to build a `ui-trigger-menu`:

```text
ui-trigger-menu
├── ui-trigger-menu-input
│   └── textarea
├── ui-trigger-menu-status
└── ui-trigger-menu-content
    ├── ui-trigger-menu-empty
    └── ui-trigger-menu-list
        ├── ui-trigger-menu-item
        └── ui-trigger-menu-item
```

`ui-trigger-menu` holds the triggers and what each one lists, set as its `triggers` property. `ui-trigger-menu-input` wraps the `<textarea>` or `<input>` people type in, and `ui-trigger-menu-content` is the popup with the suggestions. Without a `ui-trigger-menu-content` among its direct children, the menu renders the current trigger's items for you, and so does a list without items of its own. Inside a Token Input, leave out `ui-trigger-menu-input`: the menu suggests into the token input.

Parts: `<ui-trigger-menu-input>`, `<ui-trigger-menu-content>`, `<ui-trigger-menu-list>`, `<ui-trigger-menu-item>`, `<ui-trigger-menu-item-icon>`, `<ui-trigger-menu-group>`, `<ui-trigger-menu-group-label>`, `<ui-trigger-menu-separator>`, `<ui-trigger-menu-empty>`, `<ui-trigger-menu-status>`, `<ui-trigger-menu-hint>`.

members.description: The controller's methods, undefined until the element connects. `isOpen()`: Whether the menu is open. `setOpen()`: Opens or closes the menu. Opening needs a match; see `open()` for one that types the trigger. Returns false when the change was canceled or it was already open or closed. `open()`: Opens the menu for `trigger`, typing it at the caret first unless a match for it is already there, and resolves once it closes. Resolves exactly once and never rejects. `close()`: Closes the menu. The match isn't dismissed, so typing in it opens it again. Returns false when the close was canceled or it was already closed. `getQuery()`: The text after the trigger, or after the current argument's start. declarations.name: UiWaterfallElement
declarations.description:
Show a trace or a page's requests as bars on a shared time axis, with spans that expand to show what they started.

Use the following composition to build a `ui-waterfall`:

```text
ui-waterfall
├── ui-waterfall-header-row
│   ├── ui-waterfall-column-header
│   └── ui-waterfall-column-header
│       ├── ui-waterfall-axis
│       │   └── ui-waterfall-tick
│       └── ui-waterfall-mark
├── ui-waterfall-row
│   ├── ui-waterfall-row-header
│   │   └── ui-waterfall-indicator
│   ├── ui-waterfall-cell
│   └── ui-waterfall-bar
└── ui-waterfall-row
    ├── ui-waterfall-row-header
    └── ui-waterfall-bar
```

Pass every span as `items` and write a `ui-waterfall-row` for each with the span's `value`. The rows are flat siblings: the waterfall reads each one's level, place among its siblings and children from `items`. Give the waterfall an accessible name.

`ui-waterfall-row-header` names the span, and holds the `ui-waterfall-indicator` of a span with children. `ui-waterfall-bar` is the cell on the time axis. `ui-waterfall-cell` is any other column, like a status or a size. The header row, the axis and marks are optional.

Parts: `<ui-waterfall-header-row>`, `<ui-waterfall-column-header>`, `<ui-waterfall-axis>`, `<ui-waterfall-tick>`, `<ui-waterfall-mark>`, `<ui-waterfall-row>`, `<ui-waterfall-row-header>`, `<ui-waterfall-indicator>`, `<ui-waterfall-cell>`, `<ui-waterfall-bar>`.

Defined by `import "@ui-sdk/web/waterfall"`.

Part of `<ui-waterfall>`.

Defined by `import "@ui-sdk/web/waterfall"`.

Styling hooks: `data-level` (The span's depth, from 1 at the top level. Also in the `--waterfall-level` variable), `data-branch` (Present on a span with children), `data-expanded` (Present while a span with children is expanded), `data-selected` (Present on the selected span's row and its parts).

attributes.name: for
attributes.description: The id of the <ui-waterfall> it belongs to, when it isn't inside it.

attributes.name: as-child
attributes.description: Binds its first child instead of itself, like a link, and takes no box of its own.
